title: Direct activation of an innate immune system in bacteria by a viral capsid protein
authors: Zhang T; Tamman H; Coppieters’t Wallant K; Kurata T; LeRoux M; Srikant S; Brodiazhenko T; Cepauskas A; Talavera A; Martens C; Atkinson GC; Hauryliuk V; Garcia-Pino A; Laub MT
one_liner_zh: 该文研究细菌毒素-抗毒素系统通过衣壳蛋白直接激活免疫，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Bacteria have evolved sophisticated and diverse immunity mechanisms to protect themselves against a nearly constant onslaught of bacteriophages 1–3 . Similar to how eukaryotic innate immune systems sense foreign invaders through pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) 4 , many bacterial immune systems that respond to bacteriophage infection require a phage-specific trigger to be activated. However, the identities of such triggers and the mechanistic basis of sensing remain almost completely unknown. Here, we discover and investigate the anti-phage function of a fused toxin-antitoxin (TA) system called CapRel SJ46 that protects E. coli against diverse phages. Through genetic, biochemical, and structural analysis, we demonstrate that the C-terminal domain of CapRel SJ46 regulates the toxic N-terminal region, serving as both an antitoxin element and a phage-infection sensor. Following infection by certain phages, the newly synthesized major capsid protein binds directly to the C-terminal domain of CapRel SJ46 to relieve autoinhibition, enabling the toxin domain to then pyrophosphorylate tRNAs, which blocks translation to restrict viral infection. Collectively, our results reveal the molecular mechanism by which a bacterial immune system directly senses a conserved, essential component of phages, suggesting a PAMP-like sensing model for TA-mediated innate immunity in bacteria. We provide evidence that CapRels and their phage-encoded triggers are engaged in a Red Queen conflict 5 , revealing a new front in the intense coevolutionary battle being waged by phage and bacteria. With capsid proteins of some eukaryotic viruses known to stimulate innate immune signaling in mammalian hosts 6–10 , our results now reveal an ancient, deeply conserved facet of immunity.
abstract_zh: 细菌已经进化出复杂且多样的免疫机制，以保护自身免受噬菌体近乎持续的侵袭1–3。类似于真核生物先天免疫系统通过病原体相关分子模式（PAMPs）4感知外来入侵者，许多响应噬菌体感染的细菌免疫系统需要噬菌体特异性触发因子才能被激活。然而，这些触发因子的身份及其感知的机制基础几乎完全未知。在此，我们发现并研究了一个融合型毒素-抗毒素（TA）系统CapRel SJ46的抗噬菌体功能，该系统保护大肠杆菌免受多种噬菌体的侵害。通过遗传学、生物化学和结构分析，我们证明CapRel SJ46的C端结构域调控有毒性的N端区域，既充当抗毒素元件，又作为噬菌体感染传感器。在特定噬菌体感染后，新合成的主要衣壳蛋白直接结合CapRel SJ46的C端结构域，解除自抑制，从而使毒素结构域随后对tRNA进行焦磷酸化修饰，阻断翻译以限制病毒感染。总体而言，我们的结果揭示了细菌免疫系统直接感知噬菌体保守且必需组分的分子机制，提示TA介导的细菌先天免疫存在一种类似PAMP的感知模型。我们提供证据表明，CapRels及其噬菌体编码的触发因子参与了一场红皇后冲突5，揭示了噬菌体与细菌激烈共进化战斗中的新战线。鉴于某些真核病毒衣壳蛋白已知能刺激哺乳动物宿主的先天免疫信号传导6–10，我们的结果现在揭示了免疫的一个古老且深度保守的方面。
